industry.births: India's total fertility rate fell to 1.9 in 2023 (2.0 in 2021-22; replacement 2.1) and the crude birth rate to 18.4 per 1,000 (19.1 in 2022); Bihar 2.8, Delhi 1.2 (Sample Registration System 2023, reported Sep-2025). The number of births is flat to falling, so paediatric and maternity growth comes from more births in organised hospitals, higher acuity and price, not from more babies.
industry.birthsSrc: SRS Statistical Report 2023 via Outlook India (Sep-2025)
themes: Volume growth has to come from share gains, sicker babies treated privately, and new cities; deliveries grew 11% in FY26 only because Rainbow added hospitals.
Families choose hospitals with 24/7 paediatric emergency, NICU and PICU; Rainbow says standalone birthing centres cannot match this (Q1FY27 call).
Q2-Q3 are the peak; FY26's weak season cut growth to 12% from a possible 18-20% (management). The 2026 monsoon arrived late and ended ~13% below normal (IMD, 30-Sep-2026).
Rainbow added ~780 beds in two years (+40%); occupancy fell from 55% (FY23) to 46% (FY26) and 41% (Q1FY27). Listed multi-specialty chains are also adding beds in Rainbow's cities.
Insurance is ~52% of Rainbow's inpatient revenue (FY26), cash ~48%; insured patients support pricing and higher-acuity care.
Premium metros (NCR, Mumbai) and medical tourism
Higher prices and ARPOB in Gurugram and Mumbai, but higher doctor and staff costs; management sees margins above 20% in Mumbai at maturity, below the group's ~26% pre-Ind AS.
Rainbow is 'actively evaluating' government-scheme patients where beds are idle; scheme rates are lower and paediatrics is mostly medical (not surgical) care.
Competition: maternity chains and multi-specialty paediatric wings
Cloudnine is maternity-led and digital; Rainbow argues 65-70% of its business (tertiary paediatrics) is different. Large chains offer paediatrics as one department, not a dedicated network.

moat: Specialisation (paediatric multi-specialty + perinatal)
Advantage
India's largest paediatric hospital chain; ~1/3 of beds in critical care; transplants, cardiac surgery, ECMO retrieval (1,800 km Guwahati mission, Q1FY27); 3 JCI-accredited sites.
Hard to copy: a children's hospital needs dozens of sub-specialists on call 24/7.
Full-time doctor model
Advantage
1,075+ full-time doctors on retainer, working in teams, 24/7; largest private paediatric DNB training programme feeds talent.
Lower dependence on star visiting consultants; consistent care; but doctor fees are 25% of revenue.
Hub and spoke density
Advantage (in the South)
Hyderabad ~1,000 beds across 9 sites; Bengaluru ~600 beds across 6; emergency transport and referrals into hubs.
Network effects inside a city; does not travel to new cities automatically.
Brand with parents
Advantage
Mothers who deliver at BirthRight stay for paediatric care; night-time emergencies drive families to dedicated children's hospitals (management).
Sticky demand, but local, city by city.
Pricing power
Moderate
ARPOB +11% in FY26 and +6% in Q1FY27, mostly mix; mature-unit ARPOB +10% in Q1 (price and mix). Paediatrics is mostly medical care with lower ticket sizes than adult surgery.
Can raise prices 5-6% a year; not a premium surgical franchise.
Cost and scale
Parity
Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin 32% (FY26), among the highest of listed hospitals, but on a ₹1,703 cr revenue base; occupancy only 46%.
Margins come from model and mix, not from scale.
Expansion outside the South
Unproven
Guwahati (acquired) works; NCR (Rosewalk 24 beds since 2019) is still tiny; Mumbai, Pune, Indore, Gurugram hubs are new.
The moat is regional; the new markets have to be won from scratch.
Balance sheet
Advantage
No borrowings; ₹613 cr of cash and investments (Jun-2026); expansion funded from internal accruals.
Can fund ₹2,200 cr of capex over five years without equity, if cash flows hold.
critiques: Occupancy is too low: 41% in Q1FY27 and 46% in FY26 vs management's own 56-58% target; ~780 beds added in two years and ~1,200 more planned

Company decks; PL and ICICI notes flag new-unit losses

Analysts on the Q1FY27 call (HSBC, IIFL, JP Morgan)

gaps: EBITDA by hospital group (mature vs new) or by cluster is not disclosed; the margin dilution from new hospitals is described only qualitatively (breakeven in 12-18 months).
FY26 annual KPIs on the FY27 mature/new definition are not disclosed; mature/new figures are on the new basis only for Q1FY26, Q4FY26 and Q1FY27.
Pipeline hospitals' revenue in the bed build is GAM's estimate (beds × months × assumed occupancy and ARPOB); the company gives only bed counts and opening quarters.
Nellore (Prime Children's Hospital) purchase price, stake and revenue; Malad JV terms and Rainbow's stake; Guntur and Indore lease terms: not disclosed by 30-Sep-2026.
Rent for FY27-28 is our estimate (FY26 lease payments ₹95.6 cr grown with new leases); used only to translate the street's pre-Ind AS multiples.

Bank deposits for the forward EV/EBITDA history are from the FY24 and FY26 annual reports (Mar-23 to Mar-26); Mar-22 is not used (the IPO cash arrived in May-2022, so Mar-23 is used from listing to May-2023).
